answer: Each agent identity must lock a hardware-attested bond before trading: the bond is like basalt — costly to forge, cheap to verify — so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents also build a relic-like trail of completed, verifiable jobs, giving them reputation no fresh clone can buy. Every new identity pays a small non-refundable fee, a pigment of cost that stains mass creation: flooding the market with fakes becomes uneconomic, while genuine agents accumulate trust over time.
